name: Mid-Century Modern
visualIdentity: Supplemental design reference, not a directly named source-collection style. Simplified figures, organic contours and geometric color fields create a relaxed but ordered composition. Use readable poses, modest offsets and graphic transitions; optional print grain adds texture.
suitableUses: Explicitly suits illustrations and posters. The source suggests animated explainers, retro ads, title sequences, and travel, architecture or lifestyle intros when combined with compatible character movement or restrained parallax. Interactive story or chapter progression is an inferred fit, not a defining style feature.
limitations: Avoid unrelated neon and glossy plastic finishes. Keep layers flat in parallax: no blur depth of field, exposed edges, excessive separation or atmospheric gradients. Avoid paper-thickness shadows and joint gaps in cutout hybrids. Preserve supplied colors and asset colors; style combinations must retain the core palette and visual rules.
palette: Style direction: limited mustard, brick red, teal and cream; exact color count is unspecified. Suggested fallback tokens for new artwork only: background #F3E9D5, foreground #332C26, accents #C49A35, #A64E3D, #357B78. These are proposals, not canonical colors; task, brand or approved palettes take precedence. Use discrete colors; gradients are disabled. Suggested text pairs meet 4.5 contrast except cream on teal (4.095), which is decorative only. Check actual compositing; do not alter approved hues to improve contrast.
motionAndInteraction: Use modest offsets, readable poses and graphic transitions. Draw layered geometric and organic paths; fixed textures or seeded grain keep frames stable. Smooth authored motion is suitable where useful, while cuts, impacts and reading holds remain deliberate. Video state must derive from seekable composition time, not live pointer or scroll. Interactive HTML may use bounded pointer gaze, finite scroll chapter handoffs or narrative stages when scene assets support them; preserve reverse and direct seeking, reading order, keyboard/touch access and reduced-motion behavior. These are optional patterns, not style requirements.
audio: No fixed soundtrack, genre, tempo, voice or sound effect is prescribed. Choose music, narration, vocals, ambience, accents or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied assets and explicit requirements. Leave room for speech and reading, synchronize to picture, and check intelligibility, balance, clipping and timing.
assetRequirements: Draw or provide geometric and organic illustration paths; group figures and props into layers for separate movement. Grain should be fixed or seeded. Character gaze needs readable eye layers or a suitable rig; secondary brows, tilt and blinks require supported assets. Parallax needs deliberate foreground, midground and background layers with crop margins. Missing asset details are unspecified.
combinations: Cutout animation (style-084) supports hinged limbs and pose swaps at a 12 fps art cadence; use flat figures, fixed grain and readable poses. Restrained 2.5D parallax (style-101) suits layered landscapes and interiors with consistent relative speeds. Both are optional hybrids; retain the Mid-Century palette and avoid their listed craft-like shadows, gaps, depth blur or excessive separation. Other combinations are unspecified.
productionApproach: Select visual and motion methods by style and scene needs. SVG or Canvas 2D can draw the art; GSAP is the primary suggested motion engine, with Motion optional only when deterministic seeking is verified. HyperFrames owns composition, timing, media/audio sync, checks and export by default; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation prevents a required capability, and record why. It does not own style rendering. Seed randomness, drive all visual state from shared time, inspect key frames and the decoded video, and verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio sync and loop continuity. Interactive scroll or pointer behavior belongs to HTML delivery.
